newsitem.title: USA: Aames shares tumble on profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Aames shares tumble on profit warning.

text.p: The stock of Aames Financial Corp. tumbled Thursday, a day after the mortgage lender said a plan to review the pricing of loans made by third party brokers could hurt future earnings.
The stock, which traded at more than $32 in March, hit a 12-month low of $11.75 on the New York Stock Exchange. It was off $3.375, or about 22 percent, at $12 at mid-afternoon.

Aames, which announced higher third-quarter earnings late Wednesday, said it was reviewing the pricing of loans in response to changes in the mortgage market and "general uncertainties" in the bond markets where it has historically obtained funding for its operations.

Aames, which operates 51 Aames Home Loan offices in 23 states, said although the change could hurt earnings, "it will strengthen the company in the long run by improving the company's cash flow and overall financial position".

The Los Angeles-based company said its profits rose to $17.6 million, or 51 cents a share, in the third quarter from $8.6 million, or 33 cents a share, in the 1996 period. Revenues more than doubled to $84.1 million from $40.6 million.
Aames' wholly owned subsidiary, One Stop Mortgage, Inc., operates 35 offices in 31 states.
